NOTE:

 - global warming: nóng lên toàn cầu

- expand knowledge: mở rộng kiến thức

DỊCH: Tôi thường nói chuyện với bạn bè về nhiều chủ đề khác nhau liên quan đến các vấn đề xã hội như: sự nóng lên toàn cầu, chính trị,... Nói về những chủ đề như vậy không chỉ giúp chúng ta dành thời gian rảnh rỗi cùng nhau mà còn mở rộng kiến ​​thức.

parts.title: DEBATE CLUB - Part 3
parts.instructions: You are a member of a Debate Club. You are talking to other members in the club chat room. Talk to them using sentences. Use 30 – 40 words.

questions.prompt: A: Hi! Nowadays, there are many ways to update news. How do you keep up with world issues?
questions.explanation:
LỜI GIẢI: Hi. I usually read online newspapers every morning after waking up and always watch the news at 7 p.m to update the latest national and international news. Besides, I follow official pages that talk about hot issues of society on facebook.

NOTE:

     - update: cập nhật

  • latest: mới nhất
  • national: trong nước
  • international: quốc tế
  • official: chính thức
  • hot issue: chủ đề nóng bỏng

DỊCH: Xin chào. Tôi thường đọc báo trực tuyến vào mỗi buổi sáng sau khi thức dậy và luôn xem thời sự lúc 7 giờ tối để cập nhật những tin tức mới nhất trong nước và quốc tế. Ngoài ra, tôi theo dõi các trang chính thống nói về những vấn đề nóng hổi của xã hội trên facebook.

questions.prompt: B: I am going to join a debate in front of 50 people next week. How can I make a good impression?
questions.explanation:
LỜI GIẢI: I suggest that you do whatever you feel comfortable like wearing your favorite clothes or shoes. Besides, you need to have confidence and prepare what you need to say carefully on that day at home. Furthermore, it might be a good idea that you can speak loudly and clearly.

NOTE:

- speak loudly and clearly: nói to và rõ ràng

- nên dùng các liên từ như besides, furthermore, moreover,... để tăng liên kết cho câu.

DỊCH: Tôi khuyên bạn nên làm bất cứ điều gì bạn cảm thấy thoải mái như mặc bộ quần áo hoặc đôi giày yêu thích. Bên cạnh đó, bạn cần phải tự tin và chuẩn bị kỹ những điều cần nói trong ngày hôm đó ở nhà. Hơn nữa, nói to và rõ ràng là một ý tưởng hay.

questions.prompt: C: Before making a decision about something, you should consider two sides of the problem. What do you think about that?
questions.explanation:
LỜI GIẢI: I totally agree with this issue. In my opinion, everything has two sides, the good and the bad side. Therefore, I need to be very calm, usually look and think carefully before making even a small decision. That helps me a lot because it minimizes errors in my decisions.

NOTE:

  • minimize errors: giảm thiểu sai sót.
  • nên dùng các từ mang tính ý kiến cá nhân như: in my opinion, from my perspective, in my view, personally, to be honest,...

DỊCH: Tôi hoàn toàn đồng ý với vấn đề này. Theo tôi, cái gì cũng có hai mặt, mặt tốt và mặt xấu. Vì vậy, tôi cần phải hết sức bình tĩnh, thường xem xét và suy nghĩ kỹ càng trước khi đưa ra một quyết định dù nhỏ. Điều đó giúp ích cho tôi rất nhiều vì nó giảm thiểu sai sót trong các quyết định của tôi.

parts.title: DEBATE CLUB - Part 4
parts.instructions:
You are a member of a college. You received this email from the college administrator.

We want to encourage many young people to join the club, unfortunately, young people usually think that debating is not for them. What do you think is the benefit of debating and speaking in public? Please two benefits that you think are the most important and why?

questions.prompt: 1. Write an email to your friend who is also a member of the club. Write about how you feel and what you think the club should do. Write about 50 words.
questions.explanation:
Hi Phuong,

How have you been? Hope things are all good with you. Have you heard the news that our club is preparing to hold a discussion about the advantages of debate learning to recruit new members? I was so excited when hearing the news because it will attract a lot of young people to join the club. I am going to send an email to the manager of the club to give some recommendations. It (WOULD) be amazing if you could share your opinions with me. What do you reckon? Keep in touch. See you soon.

Hugs,

Linh.

DỊCH: 

Chào Phương,

Bạn thế nào rồi? Hy vọng mọi điều tốt đẹp với bạn. Bạn đã nghe CLB chúng tôi đang chuẩn bị tổ chức buổi thảo luận về lợi ích của việc học tranh biện để tuyển thành viên mới chưa? Tôi rất vui mừng khi biết tin vì nó sẽ thu hút rất nhiều bạn trẻ tham gia câu lạc bộ. Tôi sẽ gửi email cho người quản lý câu lạc bộ để đưa ra nhiều khuyến nghị. Sẽ thật tuyệt vời nếu bạn có thể chia sẻ ý kiến ​​kiến ​​trúc của mình với tôi. Bạn nghĩ sao? Hẹn giờ gặp lại sớm.

Ôm,

Linh.

questions.prompt: Write an email to the manager of the club. Write about 120 - 150 words.
questions.explanation:
Dear Sir Kien,

My name is Nguyen Thao Linh and I have been a member of this club since 2020. I received an email from our club that the club is preparing to hold a discussion about the advantages of debate learning to recruit new members. I am writing in response to your email about the news and I would like to give some opinions.

To be honest, I was very excited when I heard about the news because I have expected it for a long time. I think this is an excellent opportunity for all club members to show their eloquence and enhance their public speaking skills.

Therefore, I would like to give some recommendations. In my opinion, the benefit of debating and speaking in public is building confidence and expressing their ideas eloquently. Furthermore, I think the benefits of debating are not limited to the skills built while we are speaking, the preparation for competition teaches critical thinking and research skills.

Hopefully, my suggestions would be helpful for you. I look forward to receiving an early reply.

Yours faithfully,

Nguyen Thao Linh.

DỊCH:

Thưa ông Kiên,

Tôi tên Nguyễn Thảo Linh và tôi là thành viên của câu lạc bộ này từ năm 2020. Tôi nhận được email từ câu lạc bộ rằng câu lạc bộ đang chuẩn bị tổ chức buổi thảo luận về lợi ích của việc học tranh biện để tuyển thành viên mới. Tôi viết thư này để trả lời email của bạn về tin tức này và tôi muốn đưa ra một số ý kiến.

Thành thật mà nói, khi nghe tin này tôi rất vui mừng vì tôi đã mong đợi nó từ lâu. Tôi nghĩ đây là cơ hội tuyệt vời để tất cả các thành viên câu lạc bộ thể hiện tài hùng biện và nâng cao kỹ năng nói trước công chúng của mình.

Vì vậy, tôi muốn đưa ra một số khuyến nghị. Theo tôi, lợi ích của việc tranh luận và phát biểu trước đám đông là xây dựng sự tự tin và bày tỏ ý kiến ​​của mình một cách hùng hồn. Hơn nữa, tôi nghĩ lợi ích của việc tranh luận không chỉ giới hạn ở các kỹ năng được xây dựng trong khi chúng ta đang nói, việc chuẩn bị cho cuộc thi còn rèn luyện kỹ năng tư duy phản biện và nghiên cứu.

Hy vọng những gợi ý của tôi sẽ hữu ích cho bạn. Tôi rất mong nhận được hồi âm sớm.

Trân trọng,

Nguyễn Thảo Linh.

parts.title: TECHNOLOGY CLUB - Part 3 - V2
parts.instructions: You are a member of a Technology club. You are talking to three other members in the Technology club chat room. Talk to them using sentences. Use 30 – 40 words.

questions.prompt: A: Do you often watch movies on your laptop or go to the theater?
questions.explanation:
​​​​I usually watch movies on my laptop because watching on a laptop is not limited in time. You can watch anytime and choose your favorite movies.


DỊCH: A: Bạn có thường xuyên xem phim trên máy tính xách tay hay đến rạp?

  • ​​Tôi thường xem phim trên laptop vì xem trên laptop không bị giới hạn về thời gian. Bạn có thể xem bất cứ lúc nào và chọn những bộ phim yêu thích của mình.

questions.prompt: B. Some people prefer watching movies at home to watching in the cinema. Please give your opinion.
questions.explanation:
In my opinion, watching movies on a laptop will help us save a lot more money than going to the theater. It’s also more convenient since we don’t have to go long distances to the movie theatre.


DỊCH: Theo tôi, việc xem phim trên laptop sẽ giúp chúng ta tiết kiệm được nhiều tiền hơn so với việc ra rạp. Nó cũng thuận tiện hơn vì chúng ta không phải đi xa đến rạp chiếu phim.

LƯU Ý:

  • Dùng từ nối since/as cho tự nhiên hơn

parts.title: TECHNOLOGY CLUB - Part 4 - V2
parts.instructions:
You are a member of a Technology Club. You received this email from the club.

Dear member,

Members often post on the website’s club. But lately, there’s been a few negatives on the other member’s post. Please give your opinion to fix the situation.

questions.prompt: Write an email to your friend. Write about 50 words
questions.explanation:
Hi Linh,

We have not talked with each other for a long time. How are things? I hope you are still fine. However, lately, they sometimes make negative comments on the website. I think that can affect the reputation of my club. When I read that email, I felt down in the dumps.  I think I will send an email to give the manager of the club some suggestions to address this problem.

Love,

Nhi.


DỊCH: 

Chào Linh,

Chúng tôi đã không nói chuyện với nhau trong một thời gian dài. Mọi chuyện thế nào rồi? Tôi hy vọng bạn vẫn ổn. Tuy nhiên, gần đây một số người đã đưa ra những bình luận tiêu cực trên trang web. Tôi nghĩ điều đó có thể ảnh hưởng đến danh tiếng của câu lạc bộ của tôi. Khi tôi đọc email đó, tôi cảm thấy buồn. Tôi nghĩ tôi sẽ gửi email để đưa ra cho người quản lý câu lạc bộ một số gợi ý để giải quyết vấn đề này.

Yêu,

Nhi.

questions.prompt: Write an email to the manager of the club. Write about 120 - 150 words.
questions.explanation:
Dear Sir,

My name is Yen Nhi and I have been a technology club member for three months. I am writing this email to express my feelings and opinions about the situation REGARDING there BEING a few negatives on the member’s post.

According to the email that the club sent me last night about some negative posts. I was so sad when I heard that. ​​​​In my opinion, we should add a function to limit negative comments on the website, thus protecting the reputation and image of the club as a whole. Moreover, I would also like to suggest another idea. Anyone who has complaints about the club or other members should discuss it directly with the manager of the club. They should avoid making bad comments in public. Contacting the manager and figuring out a solution to improve the situation would be an alternative. Moreover, the administrator of the forum should pay more attention to every post’s content and apply strict censorship on this issue. 

Hopefully, my opinions are useful for you. I am looking forward to hearing your decision.

Best regards,

Doan Yen Nhi.


LƯU Ý: 

  • down in the dumps= sad
  • strict censorship: sự kiểm duyệt gắt gao
  • forum: diễn đàn
  • regarding= about
  • khuyến khích sử các từ nối: moreover, also, in addition
  • we should= i suggest we+ v nguyên thể= we ought to (c1)= it is advisable that we should
  • affect one’s reputation: làm ảnh hưởng đến danh tiếng của ai



DỊCH: 

2.Viết email cho người quản lý câu lạc bộ. Viết khoảng 120-150 từ

Xin chào ngài,

Tên tôi là Yến Nhi và tôi đã là thành viên câu lạc bộ công nghệ được ba tháng. Tôi viết email này để bày tỏ cảm xúc và ý kiến ​​của mình về tình hình LIÊN QUAN ĐẾN có một vài tiêu cực trên bài đăng của thành viên.

Theo email mà câu lạc bộ gửi cho tôi tối qua về một số bài viết tiêu cực. Tôi rất buồn khi nghe điều đó. ​​Theo tôi, chúng ta nên bổ sung thêm chức năng hạn chế những bình luận tiêu cực trên website, như vậy mới bảo vệ được danh tiếng và hình ảnh của CLB nói chung. Hơn nữa, tôi cũng muốn đề xuất một ý tưởng khác. Bất cứ ai có khiếu nại về câu lạc bộ hoặc các thành viên khác nên trao đổi trực tiếp với người quản lý câu lạc bộ. Họ nên tránh đưa ra những bình luận không hay ở nơi công cộng. Liên hệ với người quản lý và tìm ra giải pháp để cải thiện tình hình sẽ là một giải pháp thay thế. Hơn nữa, quản trị viên diễn đàn nên chú ý hơn đến nội dung mỗi bài đăng và áp dụng chế độ kiểm duyệt chặt chẽ về vấn đề này.

Hy vọng ý kiến ​​của tôi hữu ích cho bạn. Tôi rất mong được nghe quyết định của bạn.

Trân trọng,

Đoàn Yến Nhi

LƯU Ý:

  • spend hours doing smth: dành nhiều tgian làm gì mà không thấy chán
  • spend + tgian+ doing sth= sth takes sb + tgain= it takes sb+ t.gian + TO V
  • like to= love to= enjoy
  • relieve stress= unwind= let my hair down= relax= put my feet up: xả stress
  • tiring = exhausting= draining: mệt mỏi

 DỊCH: A: Bạn thích làm gì khi xem TV?

Tôi có thể dành hàng giờ ngồi trước màn hình để xem những chương trình yêu thích của mình. Tôi thích xem video ca nhạc của ca sĩ và phim hài mà tôi yêu thích để giải tỏa căng thẳng sau một ngày học tập mệt mỏi.

questions.prompt: B: Do you like watching TV alone or with others?
questions.explanation:
I like watching TV with my friend because I feel that the movie is better when we watch it together. And when I watch it alone, I will feel very bored.

DỊCH: B: Bạn thích xem TV một mình hay với người khác?

Tôi thích xem TV cùng bạn vì tôi cảm thấy bộ phim sẽ hay hơn khi chúng tôi cùng nhau xem. Và khi xem một mình tôi sẽ cảm thấy rất nhàm chán.

questions.prompt: C: Is it good for children to watch TV programs too much?
questions.explanation:
Personally, I feel that too much TV is not good for children. Because TV has so many different channels and content, when children watch it without knowing it, it greatly affects their health as well as their eyes.

 LƯU Ý: 

  • khuyến khích dùng các cụm từ mang tính cá nhân như: as far as I can remember: theo tôi nhớ, personally: theo cá nhân tôi, as far as I’m concerned= in my opinion, to be honest, from my perspective
  • as well as: cũng như là = and
  • greatly affect: ảnh hưởng rất lớn tới= have a great effect/ impact on

 DỊCH: C: Cho trẻ xem chương trình TV quá nhiều có tốt không?

Cá nhân tôi cảm thấy xem TV quá nhiều không tốt cho trẻ. Vì TV có rất nhiều kênh và nội dung khác nhau nên khi trẻ xem mà không biết sẽ ảnh hưởng rất lớn đến sức khỏe cũng như đôi mắt của trẻ.

​​Chào Hà,

Đã lâu rồi chúng ta chưa nói chuyện với nhau. Mọi chuyện thế nào rồi? Tôi hy vọng bạn vẫn đang sống tốt. Tôi vẫn ổn. Tôi đã tham gia Câu lạc bộ Khoa học được 2 tháng. Tôi nghĩ nó sẽ làm cho cuộc triển lãm trở nên thú vị và mang tính tương tác hơn. Ngoài ra, các thành viên câu lạc bộ có thể cùng nhau trang trí triển lãm dựa trên khảo sát về mức độ mong đợi của khán giả ở mọi lứa tuổi đối với sự kiện và cung cấp đồ uống, đồ ăn nhẹ cho tất cả người tham dự.

Tôi rất mong nhận được câu trả lời của bạn nếu ý kiến ​​của tôi được chấp nhận.

Thân ái,

Nguyễn Thảo.

parts.title: Reading - Test 1 - Part 5
parts.instructions:
The FIFA World Cup.


1.The inaugural competition was held in Uruguay in 1930. However, it was far smaller than present day. Firstly, only thirteen teams participated, with the majority of those being from South America. Moreover, all matches were held in the capital, Montevideo, across the city's three stadiums. While two of these existed prior to the event, they could only accommodate 10,000 to 20,000 people. Due to this, a third, Estadio Centenario, was built for an audience of 4.5 times the capacity of its predecessors. The tournament culminated in a heated final between the host country and Argentina in front of 68,000 live supporters. On home soil, Uruguay become the first World Cup champion.

2.The World Cup looks quite different today. Most remarkably, it has expanded to include a thirty-two-team roster, representing all continents. Given this vast increase in participants, it is unrealistic for all matches to be held in a singular city. The past two tournaments, in Brazil and Russia respectively, saw the inclusion of twelve different stadiums, often thousands of miles apart from one another. What's more is the size of these venues. Official regulations do not permit the grounds to hold less than 45,000 fans. Unlike its modest origin, the event is widely watched and looked forward to by billions of people worldwide. During the most recent games in Russia 2018, it is estimated that the final match between France and Croatia drew in over a billion viewers.

3.The tourney has seen participants from every corner of the globe. It has been hosted in 17 different countries on four different continents. The organization embraced its first appearance in Africa in South Africa in 2010, while Qatar is set to become the first Middle-Eastern country to host the tournament in 2022. Under some circumstances, joint countries may co-host as Japan and South Korea did in 2002, and United States, Canada and Mexico will in 2026. There have also been some notable guests along the way. For instance, the world's smallest nation to join in on the fun was Iceland, a nation with only 300,000 inhabitants.

4.What would sports be without superlatives? Brazil is the current title holder for most World Cups, with a grand total of 5. This South American nation is also the only country to have participated in every single tournament since its inception. If coming in second place had an awards category, Germany would take the lead with eight appearances in the finals, only having won 50% of those matches. Some other important achievements include performances by great athletes including Brazil's Pele, who won the most World Cup trophies by a single player, and Argentina's Maradona, who had the most appearances as a captain.

5.Hosting the event is meant to have several financial benefits, including a boost of tourism and the creation of jobs in the industrial and service sectors. However, economic waste can follow soon after. Let's consider the 2014 games as an example, where Brazil spent nearly $15 billion on developing infrastructure. Shortly after the event, it was reported that several of the multi-million-dollar stadiums were shut down due to poor construction or have been repurposed as parking lots or unsuccessful party locations. Likewise, poor planning of stadium placement has also caused venues in the Amazon region to sit vacant without the possibility of local teams or musical artists to use them.

6.Although Qatar has learned from Brazil's infrastructure problem, and vows to donate parts of their unused stadiums to developing countries after the event, the Middle Eastern nation has experienced its own share of criticism. Boiling temperatures reaching 45 degrees Celsius have been the reason for the shift of the traditionally summer-based tournament to a winter one for the first time in history. From a tourism perspective, guests will have to get used to the absence of readily-available alcoholic beverages and fewer attractions than in previous host nations. Furthermore, several human rights complaints such as the treatment of migrant workers, the illegal status of homosexuality and its political disconnection to other Middle Eastern nations are also areas of concern.

7.The issues in Qatar only scratch the surface of what is to come. In 2026, the tournament format will increase from 32 to 48 teams. This modification will help to diversify the event, granting countries who may not have otherwise qualified the chance to participate. Additionally, as the world continues to grow and change, FIFA should continue to focus more efforts to make the games more sustainable and ethical.



tentisspace

parts.instructions:
Pizza: Everything you need to know.


1.Although people have been enjoying a version of pizza since ancient times, modern pizza has its beginnings in Naples, Italy, dating back to the 18th century. Many people lived in poverty and needed food that was inexpensive to prepare and quick to consume. Tomatoes were a new commodity to Europe, and they were a cheap topping to add on to oven-baked flatbread. Other ingredients included lard, garlic and horse cheese. Due to the population’s on-the-go lifestyle, this food was often sold in the streets and eaten standing up.

2.Despite this dish being associated with the lower class, a shift in opinion occurred with King Umberto I and Queen Margherita visited the city in 1889. The pair were given an assortment of pizzas to try, but the one that won the Queen over included basil, mozzarella and tomato sauce. She loved it so much that they named the pizza after her- the Margherita. Asides from the delicious combination of flavours, the colours on the pizza represent the green, white and red of the Italian flag. Shortly after the royal couple tried this regional specialty, it became a national dish.

3.Furthermore, Italian immigrants took this recipe with them to the United States of America in the 20th century. The first pizzeria was said to have opened up in New York in 1905, fewer than 20 years after its fame in Italy. Similar restaurants in Italian-American communities began to pop up shortly after. However, the craving for pizza did not stop there. When American soldiers returned home from World War II, they desired the taste of the European delicacy they had become accustomed to while abroad. Soon, restaurants all over the nation were offering pizza on their menus.

4.As the world became more globalized, a variety of changes to suit local tastes were introduced, much to the disapproval of the original Neapolitan founders. Moving away from the traditional shape is Chicago’s deep-dish style pizza. This dish resembles a pie, where ingredients are layered in a cake pan and baked for over 30 minutes. Some of these modifications have become internationally recognized. The infamous Hawaiian style pizza, topped with pineapple and ham, was actually invented by a Greek-immigrant in Canada in the 1960s as a unique measure to attract more customers.

5.In addition to its ingredients, pizza also adapted to modern society. Chain restaurants, such as Pizza Hut and Dominos, began in the early 1960s and have spread around the world. The latter is even associated with the popularization of pizza delivery. It’s no surprise that today, Dominos operates in over 90 countries around the world. Concurrently, the invention of frozen pizza made its debut around this time. Consumers were now able to purchase a box of ready-made pizza from their local supermarket and heat it up at home at their leisure and convenience.

6.The admiration for pizza did not stop in people’s stomachs. Like its mention in classical literature, it even made it onto the big screen. Who could forget Julia Roberts in Eat, Pray, Love when she tastes pizza in Naples and professes her love for it? Even fictional characters, like the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles were also quite fond of this meal.

7.Today, its popularity is undisputed and you can find pizza all over the world. While ordering pineapple on a pizza will be met with disgust in Italy, Naples is making an effort to maintain the original form’s authenticity. In an effort to preserve the sanctity of its beloved dish, Italy has passed some laws claiming what truly qualifies as a Neapolitan pizza. This legislation specifically outlines the type of ingredients, oven and temperatures used to make the dish. Despite this, regional pizzas such as the thin-crust version in the Apulian region, or the square-cut Roman style are still allowed to exist without protest.

parts.instructions:
The Inuit


1. It is estimated that three quarters of the Inuit live in Canada’s Arctic regions, with fifty percent living in Nunavut, Canada’s biggest and newest territory. At almost 1.8 million kilometers squared, Nunavut is roughly the size of its neighbouring region, Greenland, but with half of the population density. Despite sharing land borders with three other Canadian provinces and one territory, there are no roads leading in or out. It is even home to one of the most remote communities on Earth: Alert, Nunavut. As it is less than 1000 km south of the North Pole, this unique location experiences extreme cold temperatures as well as round the clock darkness or light at each respective solstice.

2. As the Arctic conditions do not allow for agricultural success, the Inuit used to be hunter gatherers. As they travelled from place to place in search of food, these nomadic people would stay in igloos, or domed-shaped snow houses, for temporary refuge. Whales were their primary target on these hunts, as whale meat would allow these populations to sustain themselves for months. Moreover, ots oil and blubber would serve other purposes, such as providing fuel or the manufacturing of products. When the opportunity arose, they would also hunt caribou, otherwise known as a reindeer. These animals also gave the Inuit valuable fur and skins, which would be made into clothing.

3. Today, life looks quite different from that of their ancestors. The development of technology has also helped the Inuit have access to farming and agriculture. In 2014, a group of students from Ryerson University in Toronto piloted a project in the village of Naujatt to provide fresh produce for the area. A high-tech greenhouse was installed which maintains a temperature that is suitable for the cultivation of vegetables such as lettuce varieties, potatoes, legumes and so on. The project has been well-received by the community and plans for more of these greenhouses are in the works.

4. Nevertheless, life is not the easiest for the Inuit. Their geographic isolation negatively impacts their quality of life. Regardless of the small triumph of having ‘locally-grown’ agriculture, necessities such as milk and bread still have to travel thousands of kilometres before reaching an Inuit home. On average, they are still above 50% higher in price than that in the more populated provinces. A relatively high cost of living means that many of the residents of the territory are food insecure, which is ultimately connected to a vast array of health problems in these northern Indigenous communities.

5. It is also worth noting that the climate change is the biggest challenge of all. As many Inuit still use outdoor freezers to store meat, the thawing of ice means an increase of spoiled food. Rising sea levels have also been associated with more mercury in the water, which is trickled up the food chain into humans. Asides from this, global warming also poses a threat to infrastructure. As many buildings were built on partially frozen land, or permafrost, rising temperatures may cause their foundations to become structurally unstable.

6. From a traditional standpoint, this phenomenon also poses a threat to a rich Inuit history. Though it may not be a necessity for life anymore, many parents still try to show their children the ways of their ancestors. Disappearing ice means more dangerous conditions for hunting, with an increased number of experienced locals falling through the ice and drowning each year. By not being able to pass on these techniques to future generations, the Inuit will lose a unique part of their identity.

7. Some may argue that melting sea levels would bring more economic activity to the area. However, these prospects come with potentially damaging side effects. With more waterways, the tourism industry has a chance to flourish by offering cruises that would bring Canadians up north to see the Inuit way of life. An increase in cruise ships can negatively affect the ecosystems that the Inuit rely on. Moreover, there is the possibility of nearly irreversible pollution in the form of oil spills or illegal dumping from the cruise liner itself. There is no doubt that the Inuit will have to act on their changing environment, but it is vital to think about the consequences.

Education and work

Petra

As you get older, responsibilities like a job and family dominate your life. It can be hard to balance things. Studying at university is demanding. So you should do it at an age when you are independent and carefree. It is also important to learn how the world of business works. Spending unpaid time in a company is a great way to get that experience. Any course that can give you an opportunity to do that is worth considering.

Antonio

Life doesn’t really get serious until you hit your mid-twenties. Before that, try out different things and get some life experience. It’s only as you approach your thirties that you need to get serious about your career. That’s the time to start thinking about further education. Many colleges offer inexpensive courses for more mature students. Going back to student life for a year is a great idea, and you can then return to the world of work at management level.

Eleanor

Nowadays, it is popular for school leavers to take a break before they think about an occupation or a place at university. I think the most important thing is to start working as soon as you can. You need practical experience for your CV, and that can be more valuable than a diploma. Nevertheless, your studies do not have to stop just because you are working. Colleges and universities offer options for people who want to do both.

Jermaine

I think we should all keep learning, but you don’t need a piece of paper from an institution to prove it. There are many free courses available online. Of course, not all are good, but a little research will help you identify which one is best for you. A lot of young people get into debt because they have to pay for their studies. With the resources available online these days, you can take control. You won’t regret it.

parts.title: Reading - Test 5 - Part 5
parts.instructions:
Mission to Mars

1. On 3 June 2010, an international crew of six astronauts entered a spaceship and prepared themselves for a 520-day voyage to the planet Mars and back. The module that was to be their home for the next year and a half contained their sleeping quarters, a kitchen/dining room, a living room, a control room and a toilet. There was also space for food storage, a small greenhouse, a bathroom, a sauna and even a gym. The Mars landing was scheduled for 12 February 2011, following a 255-day flight, and would involve a full two days of exploration of the planet's surface. An equally long return journey would see the astronauts return to Earth on 4 November 2011.

2. Emerging from the spaceship after an exhausting 520 days, Russian commander Alexei Sitev declared the mission finally over. 'The programme has been fully carried out', he announced at a press conference. 'All the crew members are in good health. We are now ready for further tests'. Indeed, the general consensus in the scientific community was that the Mars 500 project had achieved its aims, and, what is more, the crew had managed to complete their mission without ever having to leave the earth’s atmosphere.

3. Mars 500 was, in fact, a simulation exercise. The astronauts never even left the ground, and their spaceship was a specially constructed working model situated in a warehouse in the suburbs of Moscow. The aims of the mission were to see how well humans could cope with the confinement and stress involved in extended interplanetary travel. The astronauts – three Russians, a Frenchman, an Italian and a Chinese national – were volunteers for the project, and although all of them had the option of leaving their 550-cubic metre living space at any time, none of them chose to do so.

4. All communications between the crew and mission control were subject to a twenty-minute delay to simulate the time it would take signals to reach the earth from outer space. Although not all the elements of space flight – such as the effects of zero gravity – could be reproduced, the conditions on board were made as realistic as possible. The astronauts breathed recycled air, showered only once every ten days and lived mostly on a diet of tinned food. Even the surface of Mars had been recreated to allow the crew the simulated experience of walking on the red planet.

5. In addition to the discomforts of living in a confined space, the astronauts also had to endure the psychological stresses brought about by isolation and boredom. Scientific studies have already shown that extended periods of social isolation can disrupt the normal mechanisms of the body. This can lead to increased levels of stress and higher blood pressure, which, in turn, can create feelings of anxiety and aggression. The astronauts were subject to regular medical tests throughout the experiment and they were under constant observation via a twenty-four hour closed-circuit television system. The tests continued even after the men had completed their mission as the scientists were interested to see how the astronauts would cope with a return to normal life.

6. The data collected by the experiment is further evidence that human beings are capable of overcoming the pressures of long space flight that will be necessary if future exploration of planets is to be feasible. Although there is resistance in some quarters to investment in space exploration, some scientists believe that our future lies in the stars. With the world's population exceeding seven billion and showing no sign of slowing down, future generations may be forced to seek out new worlds beyond our own increasingly overcrowded planet.

7. Although the dry and dusty landscape of Mars may not be the most suitable spot for future habitation, there are other planets that could sustain human life. To date about 700 planets with similarities to Earth have been identified outside our own solar system, and about 15 of these are potentially habitable. The most recent to be discovered – Kepler 22-b – has a surface temperature of about 22°C and orbits a star not unlike our own sun. Scientists believe that it may even contain water. However, although it may seem like a good candidate for a future space colony, it is 600 light years away, and so it is likely to remain beyond human reach for many generations to come.

parts.title: Lis Room 301 - Part 3 - Topic : Community
parts.instructions: Topic : Community
parts.passage_text:
15. Topic : Community design

- Building design can influence people’s behavior : M

Giải thích:

Man: You know, I believe building design can shape people’s behaviors and interactions from the start. When spaces are designed well, people feel comfortable and naturally start connecting.

- Creating community can take time : W

Giải thích:

Woman: Of course, design matters, but there’s no shortcut to building real community connections. Creating community takes time and consistency, even in spaces that encourage interaction.

- Work communities and social communities are the same : M

Giải thích:

Man: Really? But I also feel that work communities and social communities aren’t as different as we might think. Both require spaces that help people feel connected and valued, whether it’s at work or in social settings.

- Technology has changed how community forms : B

Giải thích:

Man: Yes, I agree, but I think technology has really changed how communities form. It makes connecting so much easier, and people don’t always need to meet face-to-face to feel a sense of connection.

Woman: I see that, but I don’t think online connections can fully replace in-person gatherings.

parts.instructions:
My neighbourhood.

Person A

I have only been living here for a few weeks, so I am still quite new to the area. So far, I am pretty impressed with all that the neighbourhood has to offer. I thought I would miss my old area a lot more, but that’s not the case. There’s a ton of nature around here. So far, I am really enjoying taking long walks through the ravine and I have also started going jogging along the path. It would be perfect if I owned a dog.

Person B

When I moved to the neighbourhood, I had the intention of going for runs around the block instead of going to the gym. However, that changed when I saw how busy the streets are in the morning. There are so many people that I feel like I am in an obstacle course trying to get past them. That’s the main reason that I really miss my old area. It was never crowded. I guess the advantage of living in a heavily-populated place is the transport links. I’ve sold my car and started taking the buses and it has saved me loads of money.

Person C

I have mixed feelings about where I live now. There is quite a big park by my house, which I thought would be perfect to walk my dogs in. However, it actually isn’t pet-friendly at all. There is no off-leash area for my pups to get some exercise. While there is a trail, it is shared by walkers and cyclists, so it could be quite dangerous for animals. Asides from that, there are very few benches and no water fountains. I think it could be so much better equipped.

Person D

I think my favourite part about my neighbourhood is the walkability. I have never owned a car and I don’t believe I will ever need one if I continue to live here. I have a small market just up the street where I buy most of my groceries. I know supermarkets tend to be cheaper to buy in bulk, but I much prefer the interaction I get in these mom-and-pop shops. There are also a few tasty family-owned restaurants all within two kilometres that are much better than any chain eatery in the city centre.

tentisspace

parts.title: Reading - Test 4 - Part 4
parts.instructions:
The Mediterranean Sea


1. Due to its connections to a plethora of different lands, the Mediterranean was a central route for trade. Not only were goods such as food products, gold and textiles transferred between and beyond ports, but cultural exchanges also occurred. To name a few, Greeks, Romans, Persians, and Ottomans all had their turn in controlling the area and this influence was expanded when trade extended to Asian countries along the Silk Road and Spice Routes. Each of these ethnic groups played an essential role in the development of Western History and the shaping of the region’s nations as we know them in modern day.

2. As a result of these mixing cultures, a common language was needed to conduct business between the merchants and travellers in the region. For this reason, Sabir, became the Lingua Franca of the region until the 19th century. That is to say, this pidgin language was a mix of the Latin-based tongues with fusions of North-African, Turkish and Greek influences, simplified in a way that people from several linguistic backgrounds were able to communicate. In spite of its abridged linguistic construction, Sabir lost its traction as respective countries began gaining more power. Today, about thirteen official languages are spoken in the area with relatively limited similarities.

3. Nevertheless, a cultural likeness in cuisine does permeate the region. While you may have heard the term, “Mediterranean Diet”, there is not a clear-cut definition of what this precisely means. Generally speaking, those who inhabit the area tend to promote a plant-based lifestyle. Instead of consuming a high proportion of red meat, they tend to incorporate a few doses of leaner options such as fish, chicken, or eggs. Unprocessed foods like fruits, veggies and legumes, as well as whole grains accompany these sources of protein. Of course, no Mediterranean meal is complete without a healthy fat, like their famous olive oil.

4. It’s not surprise that the World Health Organization recommends this lifestyle to help prevent chronic illnesses and increase lifespans. The emphasis placed on seasonal foods removes the need for processed chow. What’s more is its lack of restrictions. Bread and fats, albeit not trans or saturated ones, are welcomed in moderation. Additionally, unlike other diets, this one does not promote harmful behaviours such as calorie counting.

5. Beyond the exportation of the Mediterranean way of life, tourists flock to experience it first-hand. Having over 45,000 kilometres of breathtaking coast, millions of people visit each year. The region is home to hundreds of islands, ranging in size from the large and well-known Italian provinces of Sicily and Sardinia, to the miniscule isles of Greece. While high summer temperatures entice crowds of sunbathers, the vast array of cultural activities attract those looking to experience some of the region’s history. Likewise, tourism is vital for locals, as they heavily rely on this industry. Without it, their livelihood would be severely impacted.

6. Notwithstanding the allure of this vacation destination, human intervention is certainly taking a toll on the landscape. The overdevelopment of the Mediterranean seaside for tourism is causing the decline of biodiversity and natural coastlines. Moreover, increased pollution from cruise ships and land-based activities is quickening this process. Another major concern is overfishing. It is estimated that the majority of natural sea species in the area are heavily threatened.

7. Additionally, a humanitarian issue has become prominent in news articles regarding the Mediterranean at the present time. Dubbed a graveyard by Malta’s Prime Minister, the sea has become notorious for the deaths of many individuals. Many migrants from Africa and the Middle East trying to reach Europe have been the victims of the sea’s rough waters, enduring awful conditions and capsized ships. Whether this situation is a result of reforms to European immigration policies or not, it has gained momentum and the call for change and responsibility is widely debated among Mediterranean nations.

tentisspace

Xin chào ngài,

Tôi tên Đoàn Yến Nhi và tôi là thành viên của Câu lạc bộ Thể hình từ năm 2022. Tôi viết thư này để bày tỏ cảm xúc và những góp ý của mình về thông báo mà tôi vừa nhận được từ câu lạc bộ của chúng ta. questions.prompt: Tell me what you see from the two pictures
questions.explanation:
• Looking at the pictures, there are two women, both in the library.
  • In the first picture: There is a woman with tied short black hair in a white T-shirt standing in front of a bookshelf. She appears to be choosing a suitable book to read. Behind her stood a man, who is also looking for a book from the shelf, and there are three people in total, sitting and reading their books.
  • The second picture focused on a woman doing her academic work. She is wearing a pair of glasses and concentrating on the laptop screen, while also taking notes on her book. The setting behind her looks like the library hall with many people there.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer reading printed books or e-books?
questions.explanation:
• Although e-books are convenient and easily accessible, I still opt to read printed books.
  • I just love the feeling of holding a book in my hands, smelling the smell of paper and flipping through the pages.
  • It helps to reduce screen time and eye strain.
  • It brings me joy whenever I can come by a book from my favorite author as a reward for myself after days of hard work.

questions.prompt: Does technology affect the way we read books?
questions.explanation:
• Definitely, technology has a great impact on how we read books.
  • The advent of e-books appears to replace the role of printed books, since it is an economical investment and portable. 
  • Readers can also read books from online platforms free- of-charge or make a payment to read several books there.
  • Social media has reduced readership in our daily life, making people less interested in reading books.

parts.title: Speaking - Vội vàng - Part 4
parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me a time when you were in a hurry.
  2. How do you feel?
  3. Modern life makes us busier and more rushed. What do you think?
parts.passage_text:
1.Tell me a time when you were in a hurry.

  • Speaking of an occasion when I was in a hurry, the memory of when I attended my brother’s wedding comes to my mind.
  • As I had been living in a city a thousand kilometers from my hometown, where my brother planned to hold his wedding, I had to take a flight to get back to my hometown. 
  • Unfortunately, on my taxi heading for the airport, I completely forgot my phone at home and had to turn back to retrieve it. 
  • Luckily, I went to get the boarding check-in time, which is only 5 minutes before I missed the flight.

2. How do you feel?

  • Heading for the airport, I was worrying about missing the flight all the way.
  •  This unforgettable experience taught me to do preparations more carefully and remember to check things before leaving. 
  • I felt so lucky that I didn’t miss the flight. 

3. Modern life makes us busier and more rushed. What do you think?

  • I believe modern life makes us pressed for time and busier.
  • The competitive market leads to the rising demand among employers to perform their best at work and work overtime to contribute to the productivity and operation of their companies/ agencies.
  • Materialism is becoming prevalent, people work day and night to earn more and more money so that they can realize the ideal life of being financially secure and able to afford accommodations and settle down in big cities.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: • Looking at the picture, I can see three people: a man, a woman and a child. They must be a small family. The father has curly hair and is wearing a navy sweater, while the mother is wearing a scarf on her head with white sweater and jeans. The man is sitting on the sofa and is working on his laptop, looking very attentive, while the woman is lying on the sofa, embracing her sleeping child. The sofa is plain gray, with a beige and an orange pillow. They look so peaceful together and the room is cozy. I like this picture because it reminds me of an ideal family.

questions.prompt: Tell me the last time you worked when others slept.
questions.explanation: • The other night, I had a tight deadline for a project due the next morning. My mother, exhausted from a long day, had fallen asleep early. So I had to tiptoe into my home office and open my computer screen. While my mother was peacefully asleep in the next room, I dove into my work. As the night wore on, my eyelids grew heavy, but I pressed on, because of the urgency of the deadline. However, I was so nervous that typing the keyboard might wake my mom up in the middle of the night. Finally, just as the first light of dawn began to peek through the curtains, I put the finishing touches on my project. With a sigh of relief, I quietly shut down my computer and tiptoed back to my room, careful not to wake my sleeping mother. As I crawled into bed, I couldn't help but feel proud of my dedication and the beautiful work I had accomplished, all while my mother slept peacefully.

questions.prompt: The older we get, the more responsibility we have. Do you agree?
questions.explanation: • Yes, as we grow older, we often encounter new roles and challenges in our personal and professional lives. These can include career advancements, starting families, managing finances, and contributing to our communities. With each milestone, there's often an increase in responsibilities, and we need to face them responsibly so that we can gain greater roles and achievements in life.

parts.title: Speaking - Học kĩ năng mới - Part 3
parts.instructions: 45s/câu trả lời - trả lời từng câu

questions.prompt: Tell me what you see in the two photographs?
questions.explanation:
• In the first photo, there is a young man sitting on a couch and reading a book. He has brunette hair and a beard. He is wearing a red checkered shirt and blue jeans. He is sitting on a beige couch and is reading a book, while also holding a cup of coffee.He looks so chilled and relaxed, but also really concentrated. I like this picture because I also enjoy reading books very much.
  • In the second picture, I can see a little boy sitting in front of the computer screen. He is wearing headphones and is probably using switches to play the video game shown on the computer screen. I can not see his face but I think he enjoys it very much.

questions.prompt: How do you schedule your day to include focused studying and entertainment breaks?
questions.explanation: • I often use the Pomodoro technique, which is a great tool to help me focus better when studying. This is a structured series of shorter periods of focus that builds in time for your brain to take a break. For example, I will work hard on my academic workloads for 45 minutes and then have a 10-minute short break. This not only motivates me to focus on my study but also provides me the well-deserved break to entertain myself. This method keeps stress at bay and makes my study process more pleasant and enjoyable.

questions.prompt: Playing video games is not for adults. What do you think?
questions.explanation: • I respectfully disagree with this. Video games can be enjoyed by people of all ages, including adults. Many adults find video games to be a fun and engaging form of entertainment, and they can even provide stress relief and cognitive stimulation. It's all about personal preference and finding activities that bring joy and fulfillment. However, one should not spend too much time on video games, they should play in moderation.

parts.title: Speaking - Học kĩ năng mới - Part 4
parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me the last time you learn something new.
  2. How did you feel? 
  3. Lifelong learning is necessary for everyone. Do you agree?
parts.passage_text:
Tell me the last time you learn something new.

  • As far as I remember it was probably around when I was in high school. Back then, my English was terrible, I mean, I couldn’t understand most of what the teachers taught me. I really fell behind with my study. And as the final exam is coming, I figured out I need to do something to deal with the situation. And luckily, one of my friends recommended I register for a course at an English institution named Tentis. I decided to give it a shot because the centre has a good reputation for its innovative teaching methods. Initially, I have to admit that it was really tough from the pronunciation to the grammar, and even the vocabulary. But thanks to the patience of the teachers, I was slowly getting better with my English. I did a test in the end and I was overjoyed about the high grade I received. 


How did you feel? 

  • I gotta say that the whole experience just fostered my passion for English again, and English now has become an integral part of my life. I felt extremely delighted seeing my English getting better and my test results were higher than expected. This was a worthy investment to improve myself. Now, I really enjoy learning English and it is not difficult for me to understand its grammar and vocabulary anymore.


Lifelong learning is necessary for everyone. Do you agree? 

  • Absolutely! Lifelong learning isn't just beneficial; it's becoming increasingly necessary in today's world. Technology, society, and the economy are always changing, which means that the skills and knowledge we acquire today may become obsolete tomorrow. Therefore, committing to continuous learning ensures that we can adapt to these changes by equipping ourselves with up-to-date information and knowledge, remain competitive in the job market, and pursue new opportunities. Furthermore, in a rapidly changing global landscape, lifelong learning promotes social and cultural awareness. By actively seeking out new knowledge and experiences, we can discover new passions, deepen our understanding of the world, engage with diverse perspectives.

parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me about a time when you wanted something but couldn't have it.
  2. How did you feel about it?
  3. Material prossessions can't bring happiness. What are your thoughts on this?
parts.passage_text:
• Tell me about a time when you wanted something but couldn't have it.

There was a time when I wanted something but couldnt have it. It was my friend's birthday. At that time we were only 7 years old. Her family was wealthy and she received a lot of gifts on her birthday, which included a very costly teddy bear. I was really jealous of her since i couldnt afford one, but fortunately, she was kind enough to let me play with her teddy bear once in a while. At that time, I thought that when I grow up, I will buy everything I used to desire as a child.

  • How did you feel about it?

As a kid, I felt envious of anyone who had something that I couldn’t afford. I also felt 

self-pity and upset a lot when I didn’t own a teddy bear. However, I would soon forget about those desperate and gloomy feelings after a few days. I was also glad and grateful that my friend let me play with that teddy bear. 

  • Material prossessions can't bring happiness. What are your thoughts on this?

I partly agree with this idea for various reasons. On the one hand, people desire a lot of material possessions. For instance, some yearn for new clothes, so they go shopping; some want to eat scrumptious dishes, so they work hard to afford it. However, material possessions can't always bring us happiness. In fact, they cannot bring us quality time with our loved ones, they cannot always strengthe our relationships. Overall, I think whether material possessions can bring happiness or not depends on what one defines happiness as.

parts.passage_text:
Tell me about a time you traveled somewhere?

  • Last summer, I traveled to the beach with my family. We packed our car with swimsuits, towels, and a cooler full of snacks. After a few hours of driving, we arrived and were greeted by the sound of crashing waves and the smell of salty air. We spent the day building sandcastles, collecting seashells, and swimming in the ocean. As the sun set, we enjoyed a picnic on the sand, watching the sky turn pink and orange. It was a perfect day, full of fun and relaxation, and we all felt happy and refreshed on the drive back home.

How did you feel before the trip?

  • Before the trip, I felt excited and a little bit anxious. I was looking forward to the adventure and spending time with my family, but I also wanted everything to go smoothly. The anticipation of the fun activities we had planned and the beauty of the beach made me feel very excited and over the moon.

People spend more and more money on traveling?

  • People spend more and more money on traveling for several reasons. First, there's a trend of valuing experiences over money. Therefore, many people prioritize creating memories with their families and friends and gaining new experiences by traveling. Also, advances in transportation like airlines or metro, and many available travel options have made it easier and more affordable for people to visit many destinations around the world.

* THÍCH BỨC TRANH NÀO HƠN: I prefer picture 1 or 2 because ….

questions.prompt: Do you prefer living alone or living with your family?
questions.explanation:
+ Living with family:

- Living with my family is so comfortable cause I don’t need to care too much about electricity bills, water bills and living costs (tiền nhà). My mom cooks for me.

- Living with my family makes me feel like the luckiest person in the world. Every member shares with me a lot about work and life. I am always supported when I need someone besides me.

+ Living alone:

- Living alone makes me feel like I am leading an independent life. I have to work as hard as I can to be rich/ buy everything I need/want. I must be stronger.

- Living alone, I can do anything I want, I stay up too late and chat/ text with my friends. I can go out at midnight.

Sometimes, I feel blue and alone, I want to come back home and hug my parents.

+ Sống cùng gia đình:

- Sống với gia đình tôi rất thoải mái vì tôi không cần quan tâm quá nhiều đến tiền điện, tiền nước và chi phí sinh hoạt (tiền nhà). Mẹ tôi nấu ăn cho tôi.

- Được sống cùng gia đình khiến tôi cảm thấy mình là người may mắn nhất thế giới. Mọi thành viên đều chia sẻ với tôi rất nhiều về công việc và cuộc sống. Tôi luôn được hỗ trợ khi tôi cần ai đó bên cạnh.

+ Sống độc thân:

- Sống một mình khiến tôi có cảm giác mình đang sống một cuộc sống tự lập. Tôi phải làm việc chăm chỉ nhất có thể để trở nên giàu có/ mua mọi thứ tôi cần/muốn. Tôi phải mạnh mẽ hơn.

- Sống một mình, tôi có thể làm bất cứ điều gì tôi muốn, tôi thức khuya và trò chuyện/nhắn tin với bạn bè. Tôi có thể ra ngoài lúc nửa đêm.

Đôi khi, tôi cảm thấy buồn và cô đơn, tôi muốn trở về nhà và ôm bố mẹ tôi.

questions.prompt: Is it necessary for young people to live independently from their families?
questions.explanation:
Đọc lại câu hỏi + cụm kéo dài time + The answer is…

The answer is Yes. Living independently can be a valuable experience for personal growth. It helps people learn important skills like finance management, time management,…

Although living with family may be beneficial for young people’s mental and emotional well-being, they need to know how to take care of themselves because in the future, they will be parents.

Câu trả lời là Có. Sống độc lập có thể là một trải nghiệm quý giá cho sự phát triển cá nhân. Nó giúp mọi người học các kỹ năng quan trọng như quản lý tài chính, quản lý thời gian,…

Mặc dù sống cùng gia đình có thể có lợi cho sức khỏe tinh thần và tình cảm của những người trẻ tuổi, nhưng họ cần biết cách chăm sóc bản thân vì trong tương lai, họ sẽ làm cha mẹ.

parts.title: RECEIVING AN EMAIL (NHẬN ĐƯỢC EMAIL HOẶC THÔNG BÁO)
parts.instructions:
Tell me a time you received an email or a notification.

Which do you use to receive that email or notification?

A lot of people think that information is available these days. What do you think?
parts.passage_text:
Chia time 1p40-10-10

1. Tell me a time you received an email or a notification.

First, The last time I received an email was last night. At 11 p.m., I got an email/message from my boss about a job/work/a deadline/ a task. At that time, I was brushing my teeth before sleeping. (buổi tối) Before that, I had dinner at 7 pm. Then I watched TV at 8 p.m. I read a book at 9 p.m….

Đầu tiên, Lần cuối cùng tôi nhận được một email là vào đêm qua. Lúc 11 giờ đêm, tôi nhận được email/tin nhắn từ sếp về công việc/công việc/thời hạn/nhiệm vụ. Lúc đó tôi đang đánh răng trước khi ngủ. (buổi tối) Trước đó, tôi ăn tối lúc 7 giờ tối. Sau đó, tôi xem TV lúc 8 giờ tối. Tôi đọc một cuốn sách lúc 9 giờ tối….

2. Which do you use to receive that email or notification?

Second, When I received that email, I was using my 14 pro max, which is a smartphone from Apple/ laptop. I used it from 6 p.m to 11 p.m.

Thứ hai, khi tôi nhận được email đó, tôi đang sử dụng chiếc 14 pro max, một chiếc điện thoại thông minh của Apple/máy tính xách tay. Tôi đã sử dụng nó từ 6 giờ chiều đến 11 giờ tối.

3. A lot of people think that information is available these days. What do you think? 

Đọc lại câu hỏi + Cụm kéo dài thời gian

Finally, I don’t completely agree with this statement/opinion. I do think nowadays, it is easy to get information/news in the world/every aspect/field. But, we need to search for them. We need a laptop or a computer or a phone to do that. So I don’t think information is available. 

Cuối cùng, tôi không hoàn toàn đồng ý với nhận định/ý kiến này. Tôi nghĩ ngày nay, thật dễ dàng để có được thông tin/tin tức trên thế giới/mọi khía cạnh/lĩnh vực. Nhưng, chúng ta cần phải tìm kiếm chúng. Chúng ta cần một máy tính xách tay hoặc máy tính hoặc điện thoại để làm điều đó. Vì vậy, tôi không nghĩ rằng thông tin có sẵn.

parts.title: Speaking - LẦN LÀM ĐỒ VẬT GÌ ĐÓ MẤT NHIỀU CÔNG SỨC - Part 4
parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. The last time you made something by yourself that took a lot of effort? 
  2. How did you feel when you finished it?
  3. People should make as many items as they can instead of buying them. Do you agree?
parts.passage_text:
The last time you made something by yourself that took a lot of effort? 

I can’t remember exactly but I guess I was 20 years ago when I was a student in primary school. There was one subject called crafts, I think. And, the teacher told us to make our own wooden house. It was my very first time doing it so I was quite unsure and not ready. After hearing instructions from my teacher and with the help of my classmates, I started to do it. And it turned out that making a wooden house is not that difficult. I finally managed to finish my own house. My friends and I continuously talked and laughed during the process. In the end, my teacher awarded a prize to three students who had the most beautiful houses and luckily I was one of them.


How did you feel when you finished it?

I think it was a sense of accomplishment and I also felt proud of myself because I always thought that I was bad at doing something like DIY stuff. But that experience totally changed my mind, I had the ability to make a wooden house. It was incredible. After the class, I ran home and showed my parents what I had made and they gave compliments to me. My “piece of work” is now being displayed in the living room of my childhood home and I think I will keep it forever.


People should make as many items as they can instead of buying them. Do you agree?

No, I don’t think so. I believe each person should focus on specializing their strengths. For example, those who are good at producing clothes should produce clothes and those who are good at growing vegetables should grow vegetables. That way, everyone can create income for themselves and value for society. We will sell what we produce well and buy what we cannot make ourselves. This is how the economy is and will continue to develop.

questions.prompt: Tell me what you see in the two pictures.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits for children doing these two activities?

However, when they go to the forest, they can enjoy the nature and learn how to protect it. Both activities are great, however, I like participating in outdoor activities to gain experience and train my body.

questions.prompt: It is easier to learn something if you enjoy doing it. What do you think?
questions.explanation:
I agree that it is easier to learn something if you enjoy doing it. Because you will be more

active when learning and you can remember or understand it better. When we are interested in a topic, our brains are more engaged and motivated to learn. This can lead to increased focus, attention, and enjoyment, which in turn can make the learning process feel easier and faster.

parts.title: Speaking - Sử dụng internet - Part 4
parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me about some of the different ways you use the internet?
  2. How do you feel when you use the internet?
  3. Some people think the internet has a bad impact on our lives. What do you think?
parts.passage_text:
- Tell me about some of the different ways you use the internet?

- How do you feel when you use the internet?

- Some people think the internet has a bad impact on our lives. What do you think?

Firstly, I often use the internet to type documents or search for information for my work. Besides, I listen to music or watch online films on the internet to relax. For me, the Internet is a flexible tool which helps me to better my study as well as unwind in my leisure time. The internet can also be used for online shopping from your house and get it delivered without leaving your house. 

Secondly, I feel great when I use the internet because it can help me do everything I want.

It is very useful for both my study and work. I also use the Internet for entertainment, so I feel relaxed and happy when using it. Ever since I started using the internet, I always feel at ease as it helps my life so much easier and more convenient.

I agree that the internet has a bad impact on our lives because if people spend too much

time playing online games, it can affect their eyes and posture. Besides, excessive time spent online can lead to decreased interpersonal skills and isolation, as people may prioritize virtual interactions over real-life relationships. It also leads to mental health issues since increased screen time has been linked to higher risks of depression, anxiety, and stress.

parts.passage_text:
Tell me about a time when you achieved your goal.  

One of the biggest goals when I was younger was to pass the entrance exam to specialized highschool in my hometown. I had bent over backwards to achieve that dream. I remembered back to the time when I received the news that I passed the exam to my dream highschool. On that day, I was staying at home waiting for my exam scores when my mom called me to inform me that the results had come out. I was on pins and needles, my hands were shaking. I nervously typed my name on the highschool website to look for my scores. Fortunately, I managed to pass the entrance exam.


How do you feel about it?  

I was on cloud nine because I felt like all of my hard work had been paid off. I also felt extremely proud of myself for all the hard work and effort I have put in. 


What do people need to do to achieve their goals?  

I think they need to set clear goals first, with a clear timetable. After that, they need to be determined and stick to that timetable in order to achieve their dream.

parts.passage_text:
A time you saw an impressive work of art

  • I was once given a chance to go to a Vangogh museum, where most of his masterpieces are the main theme of the event. I then came across the painting named "Wheat Field with Cypresses" by the renowned Dutch artist Vincent van Gogh.​​​​​​ What I find most captivating about this painting is its ability to evoke a profound sense of emotion. Van Gogh's use of bold colors and dynamic brushstrokes transmits a feeling of uncertainty and passion. It also reflects his turbulent mental state at the time. I am a big fan of Vangogh’s pieces of work, so that was such a wonderful experience for me.

How did it make you feel?

  • I feel extremely impressed by the art work and also sympathetic to his pitiful life. This painting gives me a deeper insight into his story and I feel emotionally attached to it.I also felt extremely inspired by his artworks to create my own as I can express my stories and emotions without putting them into words just like Vangogh.

It is impossible to teach people to be creative. Do you agree with this ?

  • No and yes. The degree of overall creativity a person has is certainly an inherent component of a person’s inborn personality. That being said, the idea of creativity itself is a many-sided thing for which many aspects can be taught; or, at the very least, can be improved upon.

The activity took place last month in a picturesque national park known for its lush greenery and scenic trails. The day was perfect for hiking, with clear skies and a refreshing breeze. I did the activity with a group of friends from school, and we were all enthusiastic about exploring the natural beauty of the new location. The hike involved passing through a series of trails that led us through dense forests, alongside flowing streams, and eventually to a breathtaking waterfall. The experience was made even more enjoyable by the lively company of my friends, as we shared laughter, stories, and a sense of adventure.


How did you feel?

  •  I thoroughly enjoyed the outdoor activity. The combination of being surrounded by nature, the physical exertion of the hike, and the memories with friends created a joyful and memorable experience. The outdoor hiking activity in the new national park was a source of great happiness. It provided a perfect blend of nature, physical activity, and shared moments with friends, making it an experience I truly relished.


What are some advantages of getting close to nature? 

  • Spending time in green space or bringing nature into your everyday life can benefit both your mental and physical wellbeing. For example, doing things like growing food or flowers, exercising outdoors or being around animals can have lots of positive effects. Nature can help decrease your anxiety levels and can help lessen stress and feelings of anger, as well as lower risks of depression and improve concentration and attention.

questions.explanation:
• Giống: Both pictures show places to eat/eating places. 
  • Khác:

In the first picture,...

But in the second picture,...

Regarding the differences, in the first picture, it is a popular restaurant/ a low-cost restaurant, in contrast, in the second picture, it is a high-class restaurant. 

  • Thích tranh nào hơn: I prefer picture 2 because I always have money to burn. 

Cả hai hình ảnh hiển thị những địa điểm ăn uống.

Trong bức tranh đầu tiên,...

Nhưng ở bức tranh thứ hai,...

Về sự khác biệt, ở hình 1 là quán bình dân/ bình dân, ngược lại ở hình 2 là nhà hàng cao cấp.

Tôi thích hình 2 hơn vì tôi luôn có tiền để đốt, tiêu xài.

questions.prompt: What would it be like to eat in two places?
questions.explanation:
In a low-cost restaurant, we are offered a more budget-friendly and casual dining experience. The first place (pic 1) often has simpler menus. It means the dish may be basic and familiar. In addition, the atmosphere is designed to cater to a wide range of customers.

In a high-class restaurant, we can expect a more luxurious dining experience with a strong emphasis on quality and service. It offers a diverse and sophisticated menu and dishes are beautifully presented. The chefs need to focus on using high-quality ingredients and innovative cooking techniques. Service in a high-class restaurant is top-notch and often has staff members attending to customers’ needs. 

Trong một nhà hàng bình dân, chúng ta được cung cấp trải nghiệm ăn uống bình dân và hợp túi tiền hơn. Địa điểm đầu tiên  (ảnh 1) thường có menu đơn giản hơn. Có nghĩa là món ăn có thể cơ bản và quen thuộc. Ngoài ra, không khí nhà hàng được thiết kế để phục vụ cho nhiều đối tượng khách hàng.

Trong một nhà hàng cao cấp, chúng ta có thể mong đợi một trải nghiệm ăn uống sang trọng hơn với sự tập trung về chất lượng và dịch vụ. Nó cung cấp một thực đơn đa dạng và tinh tế, các món ăn được trình bày đẹp mắt. Các đầu bếp cần tập trung vào việc sử dụng nguyên liệu chất lượng cao và kỹ thuật nấu ăn độc đáo sáng tạo. Dịch vụ trong một nhà hàng cao cấp là hàng đầu và thường có nhân viên phục vụ nhu cầu của khách hàng.

questions.prompt: Which of the two places would be healthier to eat in? Why?
questions.explanation:
It depends on a variety of factors including cooking methods, ingredients used, and menu options. However, high-class restaurants often prioritize quality ingredients and more diverse options. Portions there are typically smaller which can help control the amount of food we eat. 

Điều đó phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố bao gồm phương pháp nấu ăn, nguyên liệu được sử dụng và các lựa chọn trong thực đơn. Tuy nhiên, nhà hàng cao cấp thường ưu tiên nguyên liệu chất lượng và lựa chọn đa dạng hơn. Các phần ăn thường nhỏ hơn có thể giúp kiểm soát lượng thức ăn chúng ta ăn.

parts.title: Speaking - NHẬN MÓN QUÀ - Part 4
parts.instructions:
2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me a time you received a gift.
  2. How do you feel about this gift?
  3. Why do people give gifts?
parts.passage_text:
1. Tell me a time you received a gift.

The time that I received a gift was on my 18th birthday. My parents bought a car for me. My car is a Roll-Royce which is so expensive that only rich/wealthy people own it.

+Mô tả về quà: Only a few cars were sold worldwide because this model is a limited edition.

+Bối cảnh diễn ra: (thêm 1 ngày).

Lần mà tôi nhận được một món quà là vào ngày sinh nhật thứ 18 của tôi. Bố mẹ tôi đã mua một chiếc ô tô cho tôi. Xe của tôi là một chiếc Roll-Royce đắt đến mức chỉ những người giàu có mới sở hữu nó.

+Mô tả về quà tặng: Chỉ có một số ít xe được bán ra trên toàn thế giới vì đây là phiên bản giới hạn.


2. How do you feel about this gift?

Over the moon, grateful to my parents, and need to try my best to be rich like my parents,…

I was jumping for joy when I received this priceless gift. I felt grateful to my parents and told myself to try my best to be a savvy businessperson like my Dad. 

Sung sướng, biết ơn bố mẹ, cần phải cố gắng hết sức để giàu có như bố mẹ, …

Tôi đã nhảy cẫng lên vì sung sướng khi nhận được món quà vô giá này. Tôi cảm thấy biết ơn bố mẹ và tự nhủ phải cố gắng hết sức để trở thành một doanh nhân hiểu biết như bố tôi.


3. Why do people give gifts?

People give gifts for a variety of reasons.

  • Express their feelings/love

One of the primary reasons for giving gifts is to express love, affection, and appreciation to someone. It means gifts can convey emotions/messages that words alone may not capture. 

  • On special occasions

Gifts are often given to mark significant life events such as birthdays, weddings, anniversaries, and graduation that help celebrate and make these occasions memorable. 

  • Strengthen relationships

Gift-giving can foster relationships and be a way to nurture connections between people. 

Mọi người tặng quà vì nhiều lý do.

  • Thể hiện cảm xúc / tình yêu.
  • cảm xúc/thông điệp mà chỉ lời nói không thể nắm bắt được.
  • Vào những dịp đặc biệt

Quà tặng thường được tặng để đánh dấu các sự kiện quan trọng trong đời như sinh nhật, đám cưới, ngày kỷ niệm và tốt nghiệp để giúp kỷ niệm và làm cho những dịp này trở nên đáng nhớ.

  • Thắt chặt các mối quan hệ

Tặng quà có thể thúc đẩy các mối quan hệ và là một cách để nuôi dưỡng sự kết nối giữa mọi người.

2 phút/ 3 câu - trả lời liên tục

  1. Tell me about a time when you worked in a team.  
  2. How do you feel when you work in a team?  
  3. What are the advantages of teamwork?
parts.passage_text:
Tell me about a time when you worked in a team.  

  • I worked on a sales team where we needed to increase our monthly sales. I started a weekly meeting where the team could brainstorm and share our ideas for innovating and finding new sales tactics. I worked with colleagues to put these ideas into presentations, which we delivered to managers.

How do you feel when you work in a team?  

  •  Being part of a great team at work is an amazing feeling. You feel excited, challenged and safe at the same time. It also keeps you energized and pumped up throughout the day. 

What are the advantages of teamwork?  

  • Strong team dynamics enable individual members to divide complex projects into manageable tasks, which enhance productivity and enable an organization to function more effectively. Moreover, successful teamwork creates a supportive network that can significantly enhance job satisfaction and employee morale.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture
questions.explanation:
In the picture is a group of 7 people in a very nice room. There was a man dressed very neatly standing and speaking in front of people. This man's demeanor is very calm and confident. There are many papers and files on the table. I guess they were presenting about some important project.

I remember I used to be like that before. I am also very confident speaking in front of people.

Trong hình là một nhóm gồm 7 người trong một căn phòng rất đẹp. Có một người đàn ông đang mặc rất chỉnh tề và đứng nói trước những người còn lại. Phong thái của người đàn ông này rất điềm tĩnh, tự tin. Trên bàn có rất nhiều giấy tờ và hồ sơ. Tôi đoán là họ đang thuyết trình về một dự án quan trọng nào đó.

Tôi nhớ lại trước kia tôi cũng đã từng như vậy. Tôi cũng rất tự tin nói trước đám đông.

questions.prompt: Tell me the last time you spoke in front of a lot of people.
questions.explanation:
• The last time spoke in front of a lot of people was 5 months ago.
  • When presenting initial emotions: shy, worried, scared,...Later, calm down, confident.
  • After the presentation that day, I felt like I had become a different person.

The last time I spoke in front of a lot of people was 5 months ago. When I was a leader in a group. This is the first time I have been the leader and present in front of a lot of people. First, I felt shy, worried about, and scared,.. because many people follow me and they were evaluating my actions when I spoke. Later, I was calm down and confident,...because I was preparing it very carefully. I spoke smoothly, about how to emphasize important points. Finally, the presentation was successful and many people complimented me. After the presentation that day, I became more confident, bolder and transformed myself into a different person to be more successful.

Lần cuối cùng tôi nói trước nhiều người là vào 5 tháng trước. Khi ấy tôi là trưởng nhóm. Đây là lần đầu tiên tôi trong vai trò lãnh đạo và thuyết trình trước mọi người. Ban đầu, tôi cảm thấy ngại, sợ, lo lắng,.. bởi vì có rất nhiều người theo dõi và đánh giá những hành động khi tôi nói. Về sau, tôi cảm thấy bình tĩnh, tự tin,.. bởi vì tôi đã chuẩn bị nos cẩn thận. Tôi nói rất mượt, biết nhấn nhá những điểm quan trọng. Cuối cùng, bài thuyết trình diễn ra tốt đẹp và nhiều người đã dành lời khen cho tôi. Sau buổi nói ngày hôm đó tôi có thêm nhiều tự tin hơn, mạnh dạn hơn và tự biến mình thành một con người khác để thành công hơn.

questions.prompt: Why do people usually feel worried when speaking in front of many people?
